title: The Many Missed Warnings Before Maine’s Mass Shooting

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，《纽约时报》记者。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the mass shooting that occurred in May last week, killing 18 people, was the country's deadliest of the year.
sentences.zh: 今天，上周五月发生的这起导致18人死亡的大规模枪击事件，是今年美国国内致死人数最多的一次。

sentences.en: It may also have been one of the most avoidable.
sentences.zh: 它也可能是最完全可以避免的事件之一。

sentences.en: My colleague, Nicholas Bogle-Burrows, on why so many warnings about the suspected gunman from so many people failed to stop it.
sentences.zh: 我的同事尼古拉斯·博格尔-伯罗斯将为我们讲述，为什么这么多人曾就这名疑似枪手发出过那么多警告，却没能阻止悲剧的发生。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, November 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月2日，星期四。

sentences.en: Nick, in the days since this awful mass shooting in Maine, you have been trying to reconstruct the warning signs that something was very wrong with the suspected shooter.
sentences.zh: 尼克，在缅因州发生这起可怕的大规模枪击事件之后的几天里，你一直在试图还原那些表明这位嫌疑人存在严重问题的危险信号。

sentences.en: So tell us about what you have been finding.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲你都有了什么发现吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in the days after this attack, we've received a bunch of documents that show a series of troubling interactions with the suspect, whose name is Robert Card.
sentences.zh: 好的，在这起袭击发生后的几天里，我们收到了一堆文件，显示了与嫌疑人罗伯特·卡德之间一系列令人不安的互动。

sentences.en: He's a 40-year-old Army reserviSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一名40岁的陆军预备役军人。

sentences.en: And the documents show that these warnings concerned his deteriorating mental health, rising paranoia and anger, and they came from pretty much every part of his life.
sentences.zh: 文件显示，这些警告涉及他日趋恶化的心理健康、不断上升的偏执和愤怒，而且这些警告几乎来自他生活的方方面面。

sentences.en: But as we now know, none of those warnings prevented this mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们现在所知，所有这些警告都没有阻止这场大规模枪击事件的发生。

sentences.en: Well, Nick, where should we start in the story of those warnings?
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，关于这些警告的故事，我们应该从哪里开始说起呢？

sentences.en: You mentioned that they go back many months.
sentences.zh: 你提到它们可以追溯到好几个月前。

sentences.en: I mean, the first time when the local police are really made aware that this guy is a concern is about five months ago in May,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当地警方真正意识到这个人是个隐患，最早是在大约五个月前的五月份，

sentences.en: when his ex-wife and teenage son go to a school resource officer.
sentences.zh: 当时他的前妻和十几岁的儿子去找了一名学校资源警官。

sentences.en: And the school resource officer calls down a sheriff's deputy to speak with the family.
sentences.zh: 然后，学校资源警官叫来了一名治安官副警长与这家人谈话。

sentences.en: And in that interview, the teenage son and the ex-wife say that he has started to hear voices.
sentences.zh: 在那次谈话中，十几岁的儿子和前妻说他开始听到幻听了。

sentences.en: He started to be increasingly paranoid and angry.
sentences.zh: 他开始变得越来越偏执和愤怒。

sentences.en: They also note he has collected about 10 to 15 guns that he kept at a relative's house and brought them back to his.
sentences.zh: 他们还指出，他收集了大约10到15支枪，原本放在亲戚家，后来被他拿回了自己家。

sentences.en: So they're going to the police and saying that he has access to a large number of firearMs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去找警察，说他能接触到大量的枪支。

sentences.en: I mean, they were very worried about him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对他的情况非常担忧。

sentences.en: And I think what they also were struggling with is not understanding where to get him help and what kind of intervention might lead him to be more aggressive and more isolated.
sentences.zh: 我想他们当时也在苦恼，不知道该去哪里为他寻求帮助，也不知道什么样的干预措施可能会导致他变得更具攻击性、更加孤立。

sentences.en: So what's the response from the local police after the family has this conversation with them?
sentences.zh: 在这家人与警方进行这次谈话后，当地警方的反应是什么？

sentences.en: The deputy has this conversation with the ex-wife and the teenage son and seems to talk to them at length and learn a lot about Card's behavior and his career in the Army Reserves.
sentences.zh: 副警长与前妻和十几岁的儿子进行了谈话，似乎与他们进行了长时间的交流，并深入了解了卡德的行为以及他在陆军预备役的职业生涯。

sentences.en: He was in the Army Reserves for 20 plus years at that point.
sentences.zh: 那时他在陆军预备役已经待了20多年了。

sentences.en: And the deputy and the ex-wife basically decide that the best place to get help is probably through the Army Reserve.
sentences.zh: 副警长和前妻基本上认为，寻求帮助最好的途径可能还是通过陆军预备役。

sentences.en: It's people who have known him for a long time.
sentences.zh: 那里的人认识他很久了。

sentences.en: It's people he interacts with regularly.
sentences.zh: 那是他经常互动的人。

sentences.en: And maybe they have a more formal system of getting someone like this help.
sentences.zh: 也许他们有一套更正式的系统来为这样的人提供帮助。

sentences.en: So the deputy goes back and makes a call to the Army Reserve base and learns from them.
sentences.zh: 于是，副警长回去给陆军预备役基地打了电话，并从他们那里了解了情况。

sentences.en: And this is in May that they've been aware of his declining mental health at the Army Reserve base and that they already know that something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 早在五月份，陆军预备役基地就已知晓他不断恶化的心理健康状况，并且他们已经知道情况不对劲了。

sentences.en: So at this point, they have two really important data points.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，他们掌握了两个非常重要的信息点。

sentences.en: They have family members deeply concerned that this man is not well and has guns.
sentences.zh: 他们有家属深深担忧这个男人状态不佳且拥有枪支。

sentences.en: And they now know that his place of work, the Army Reserves, is also very concerned about him.
sentences.zh: 他们现在还得知，他的工作单位陆军预备役也非常担心他。

sentences.en: So what do the police do with all this information?
sentences.zh: 那么警察对所有这些信息做了什么处理？

sentences.en: They decide, I think, largely to leave it in the Army Reserve's hands.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们基本上决定把这件事交由陆军预备役处理。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the police come up with a kind of informal solution to this problem, which is work with the Army Reserves.
sentences.zh: 所以警方想出了一个解决这个问题的非正式方案，那就是与陆军预备役合作。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So the next thing we know that happens is in July.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的接下来发生的事是在七月份。

sentences.en: Card travels with his reserve unit to West Point, New York, for an annual training exercise.
sentences.zh: 卡德和他的预备役部队一起前往纽约州西点军校参加年度训练演习。

sentences.en: And there's a very concerning incident that takes place.
sentences.zh: 期间发生了一起非常令人担忧的事件。

sentences.en: They're all hanging out together at a motel.
sentences.zh: 他们当时一起在一家汽车旅馆里闲逛。

sentences.en: And he starts accusing them of calling him a pedophile.
sentences.zh: 他开始指责他们叫他恋童癖。

sentences.en: This is one of his paranoid delusions that comes up repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 这是他反复出现的偏执妄想之一。

sentences.en: He shoves one at one point, and everyone is just freaked out.
sentences.zh: 有一次他推搡了其中一个人，所有人都被吓坏了。

sentences.en: And eventually they call for a supervisor who comes down and tries to speak with Card in his motel room.
sentences.zh: 最后他们找来了一位主管，主管来到卡德的汽车旅馆房间试图和他谈谈。

sentences.en: Card tries to slam the door on him.
sentences.zh: 卡德试图当着他的面把门关上。

sentences.en: So the supervisor decides that Card needs medical attention.
sentences.zh: 于是主管认为卡德需要接受医疗护理。

sentences.en: He takes him to a hospital, and he later writes about a concerning interaction during that time where Card was just staring at him for four hours or through him without blinking.
sentences.zh: 他把他带到了医院，后来主管记录了当时一段令人担忧的互动：卡德只是死死地盯着他看了四个小时，或者说眼神空洞地看着他，连眼睛都不眨一下。

sentences.en: And at the hospital, they ultimately decide that he needs further treatment and that he should be moved to a psychiatric center, which he is.
sentences.zh: 在医院里，他们最终决定他需要进一步治疗，应该被转移到精神病中心，而他也确实被转了过去。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what do we know about the kind of treatment he receives there?
sentences.zh: 我们对他在那里接受的治疗有什么了解吗？

sentences.en: We know next to nothing except the amount of time he spent there, which was 14 days.
sentences.zh: 除了他在那里待的时间——14天之外，我们几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that after two weeks, he left, and that his supervisor in the reserve say that they're not sure he ever sought treatment again.
sentences.zh: 两周后他离开了，他在预备役的主管说他们不确定他是否再次寻求过治疗。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is clearly a very delicate moment in the story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这显然是整个事件中非常微妙的一个时刻。

sentences.en: He's very unwell.
sentences.zh: 他的精神状况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Everyone's aware of it.
sentences.zh: 所有人都意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: He's just come out of a hospital.
sentences.zh: 他刚刚从医院出来。

sentences.en: What happens to him?
sentences.zh: 他后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: The next thing we know is that in the days after he was released from this psychiatric center, he tries to pick up a silencer for a gun that he had bought.
sentences.zh: 我们所了解到的下一件事是，在他从精神病中心释放后的几天里，他试图去取他买的一支枪的消音器。

sentences.en: Interestingly, on that form, to pick that up, it asks if he has had a mental health treatment or been committed for mental health treatment.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在提取该物品的表格上，询问了他是否接受过心理健康治疗，或者是否因心理健康治疗而被强制收治。

sentences.en: And he actually answers yes.
sentences.zh: 而他居然回答了“是”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He's up front and says he has.
sentences.zh: 他很坦诚地承认了。

sentences.en: And so the gun shop owner says, I can't give this to you.
sentences.zh: 所以枪店老板说：“我不能把这个给你。”

sentences.en: And he's, from what we heard, very nice about that and says, okay, no problem.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，他对此态度很好，说：“好的，没问题。”

sentences.en: I'll figure that out and never comes back.
sentences.zh: “我自己想办法，”然后就再也没有回来。

sentences.en: After that, things just go downhill.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，情况急转直下。

sentences.en: In mid-September, he is riding in a car with a longtime friend and fellow reservist and starts talking in very concerning ways.
sentences.zh: 在9月中旬，他和一位多年的老友兼预备役战友坐在一辆车里，开始说一些非常让人担忧的话。

sentences.en: He's saying that he's upset with people calling him a pedophile, but he also starts talking about carrying out a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 他说他对别人叫他恋童癖感到很不高兴，但他也开始谈论要实施大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He starts talking about shooting up places, including his Army Reserve base and other establishments.
sentences.zh: 他开始谈论要去一些地方开枪扫射，包括他的陆军预备役基地和其他场所。

sentences.en: And at one point, his friend who's in the car says something like, you need to stop talking like that or you're going to get in trouble.
sentences.zh: 有一次，坐在车里的朋友说了一句类似“你别这么说话，不然你要惹上麻烦了”这样的话。

sentences.en: And Card actually punches him in the face.
sentences.zh: 结果卡德竟然一拳打在了他的脸上。

sentences.en: So his friend gets out of the car, makes his way home, and then contacts their superiors in the reserve and says he's worried about his friend.
sentences.zh: 于是他的朋友下了车，设法回到了家，然后联系了预备役的长官，说他很担心自己的朋友。

sentences.en: And what do the reserves do in response to that?
sentences.zh: 预备役对此做出了什么反应？

sentences.en: So this initiates basically, I think, the most intense intervention that we've seen at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上引发了我认为迄今为止我们见过的最强烈的干预。

sentences.en: The reserves reach out to the sheriff's office in Sagahawk County, where Card lived.
sentences.zh: 预备役联系了卡德居住的萨加哈克郡治安官办公室。

sentences.en: So the same sheriff's office, right, Nick, that the son and ex-wife have been talking to?
sentences.zh: 就是尼克你刚才说的那个其儿子和前妻一直在与之沟通的同一个治安官办公室，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this sheriff's office knew about concerns back in May, and now they're hearing from the Army Reserve in September that things have escalated.
sentences.zh: 所以这个治安官办公室早在五月份就知道这些担忧了，现在他们在九月份又从陆军预备役那里听说情况已经升级了。

sentences.en: So the reserve says, we'd like you guys to go check on this guy, basically perform a welfare check.
sentences.zh: 于是预备役说：“我们希望你们去查看一下这个人的情况，基本上就是进行一次福利查访。”

sentences.en: So the sheriff's sergeant goes back to Card's address, and there are indications that he might be home.
sentences.zh: 于是治安官中士再次前往卡德的住址，有迹象表明他可能在家。

sentences.en: So the sheriff's sergeant calls for backup.
sentences.zh: 于是治安官中士请求了支援。

sentences.en: They try to make contact with Card.
sentences.zh: 他们试图与卡德取得联系。

sentences.en: They go up to his door.
sentences.zh: 他们走到了他的门前。

sentences.en: They think they might hear him moving around inside, but he won't come to the door.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己可能听到他在屋里走动的声音，但他就是不肯开门。

sentences.en: And so at that point, they decide, because they're in a sort of, as they describe it, disadvantageous position, fearing that he's armed and unwell, they decide to leave him
sentences.zh: 所以在那种情况下，由于他们处于他们所形容的某种不利位置，担心他持有武器且精神状态不佳，他们决定在当时暂时

sentences.en: alone at that point.
sentences.zh: 不再打扰他。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: That's kind of a confounding place for police to land, because at this point, this sheriff's office knows very well that multiple people on multiple occasions have determined that
sentences.zh: 这对警方来说是一个挺让人匪夷所思的结局，因为在这个时候，这个治安官办公室非常清楚，有多人在多个不同场合已经判定

sentences.en: this man is a threat.
sentences.zh: 这个人是个威胁。

sentences.en: Sounds like the police officers outside the house themselves think he's a threat.
sentences.zh: 听起来房子外面的警察自己也认为他是个威胁。

sentences.en: So they just leave, you're saying, even though all signs point to someone whose mental state
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，他们就这么走了，尽管所有迹象都表明此人的精神状态

sentences.en: has gotten worse and worse and worse, and who's now explicitly making threats of shooting people.
sentences.zh: 变得越来越糟糕，而且现在已经明确扬言要枪杀他人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They do leave the home, and the sheriff's sergeant goes back and starts to reach back out to
sentences.zh: 他们确实离开了住所，治安官中士回去后开始重新联系

sentences.en: Card's family and his reserve base.
sentences.zh: 卡德的家人和他的预备役基地。

sentences.en: I think at this point, he's trying to learn a little bit more about what might be going on.
sentences.zh: 我想此时他正试图进一步了解可能正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So the sheriff's sergeant reaches out to an army reserve captain who knows Card, and the captain says he thinks that trying to force a contact is a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 于是治安官中士联系了一位认识卡德的陆军预备役上尉，这位上尉表示他认为强行接触是个坏主意。

sentences.en: He actually recommends to the sheriff's office that they just leave him alone.
sentences.zh: 他实际上建议治安官办公室直接别去管他。

sentences.en: And he says, it's maybe just best to let Card have time to himself for a bit.
sentences.zh: 他说，也许最好让卡德独自独处一段时间。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: At that point, the sheriff's sergeant calls Card's brother, and the brother says that he will try to take Card's guns away.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，治安官中士给卡德的兄弟打了电话，其兄弟表示他会设法把卡德的枪收走。

sentences.en: He says that they have a way to secure the weapons, and he's going to work with their dad to try to make sure that Card doesn't have any access to his guns.
sentences.zh: 他说他们有办法保管这些武器，他将和他们的父亲合作，确保卡德无法接触到他的任何枪支。

sentences.en: And that's where the sheriff's office leaves it.
sentences.zh: 治安官办公室就这样把事情搁置了。

sentences.en: And, you know, by mid-September, they've never made contact with Card himself.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，直到9月中旬，他们都从未与卡德本人有过接触。

sentences.en: The sheriff's office never met with him, and they never do.
sentences.zh: 治安官办公室从未与他会面，后来也一直没有。

sentences.en: And then, in October, he buys more guns legally, and then, within days, he goes to a bar and a bowling alley in Lewiston, Maine, and opens fire.
sentences.zh: 然后，在10月份，他合法购买了更多的枪支，接着在几天之内，他去了缅因州刘易斯顿的一家酒吧和一家保龄球馆开枪射击。

sentences.en: And he kills 18 people and wounds 13 more.
sentences.zh: 他杀死了18人，并打伤了另外13人。

sentences.en: Nick, the layers of warnings that you have discovered in your reporting and outlined in the first half of our conversation are breathtaking.
sentences.zh: 尼克，你在报道中发现并在我们对话前半部分梳理出的层层警告，简直令人震撼。

sentences.en: And yet, none of that stopped this man from either buying guns or being forced to give up the guns that he had.
sentences.zh: 然而，所有这些都没有阻止这个人购买枪支，也没有迫使他交出手中的枪支。

sentences.en: And I'm emphasizing that because even within the very emotional gun control debate that's always raging in this country, lawmakers from both parties have generally agreed that
sentences.zh: 我之所以强调这一点，是因为即使在这个国家历来争论不休、充满情绪化的控枪辩论中，两党议员通常也一致认为

sentences.en: there's a need for ways to take guns from people who pose a threat, mostly because of their mental health.
sentences.zh: 有必要采取途径没收那些构成威胁的人的枪支，这主要是基于他们的精神健康考虑。

sentences.en: Does Maine have such a law, and how did it operate or fail to operate in this case?
sentences.zh: 缅因州有这样的法律吗？在这起案件中，它又是如何运作或失效的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Maine is an interesting state politically.
sentences.zh: 是的，缅因州在政治上是一个很有趣的州。

sentences.en: Its government is controlled by Democrats.
sentences.zh: 它的政府由民主党控制。

sentences.en: It has a Democratic governor.
sentences.zh: 它有一位民主党州长。

sentences.en: But on the issue of guns, it's more complicated.
sentences.zh: 但在枪支问题上，情况更加复杂。

sentences.en: There's a large hunting culture here.
sentences.zh: 这里有着浓厚的狩猎文化。

sentences.en: And in part for that reason, the state has a history of resisting certain gun control laws.
sentences.zh: 部分也是因为这个原因，该州历史上一直抵制某些枪支管控法律。

sentences.en: But Maine does have a law that went into effect in 2020.
sentences.zh: 但缅因州确实有一项在2020年生效的法律。

sentences.en: That law is called a yellow flag law.
sentences.zh: 这项法律被称为“黄旗法”。

sentences.en: And it's basically a compromise.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一种妥协的产物。

sentences.en: And so the yellow flag law in Maine is different than red flag laws in other states, which allow
sentences.zh: 所以缅因州的黄旗法与其他州的红旗法不同，其他州的红旗法允许

sentences.en: families to go straight to a court and ask them to take away someone's guns because they're worried about them.
sentences.zh: 家属直接去法院，要求法官因为担心某人的状况而没收其枪支。

sentences.en: In Maine, the yellow flag law requires that the police get the person evaluated by a medical
sentences.zh: 而在缅因州，黄旗法要求警方让医疗人员对该人员进行评估，

sentences.en: practitioner, and then they take that evaluation and go to a court and then hope that a judge will sign off on them being able to take their weapons away.
sentences.zh: 然后拿着这份评估结果去法院，并寄希望于法官能够批准他们没收其武器的请求。

sentences.en: It adds that extra step of needing to go to a medical practitioner and have an evaluation done.
sentences.zh: 它增加了需要找医疗人员进行评估这一额外的步骤。

sentences.en: And it also keeps families from being able to directly ask a court to take away someone's guns.
sentences.zh: 并且它也阻止了家属直接向法院申请没收某人枪支的权利。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So just to clarify, yellow flag law is a little bit more cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 所以澄清一下，黄旗法要繁琐一些。

sentences.en: Sounds like it's also more time consuming, involves more steps and more parties, which is why perhaps you described it as a compromise.
sentences.zh: 听起来它也更耗时，涉及更多的步骤和更多的方方面面，这也就是为什么你刚才把它描述为一种妥协。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it's a little bit more of a watered down version of a red flag law, which makes it a bit easier to take away someone's guns.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，它可以说是红旗法的一个稍微淡化版本，这使得没收某人的枪支变得稍微困难了一点。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So did anyone try to use Maine's yellow flag law in the case of this man?
sentences.zh: 那么在这名男子的案件中，有没有人试图使用缅因州的黄旗法呢？

sentences.en: No, there's no indication that anyone tried to use that law.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有任何迹象表明有人试图动用该法律。

sentences.en: The police could have decided that it was worth taking card to a medical practitioner trying to get him evaluated and then go to a judge to force him to give up his guns.
sentences.zh: 警方本可以决定带卡德去看医疗从业人员、试图对他进行评估，然后去找法官强制他交出枪支，这绝对是值得去做的。

sentences.en: But no one took that step.
sentences.zh: 但没有人采取这一步。

sentences.en: I'm really curious what we know about why the police department didn't try to use the yellow flag law, because it clearly exists to solve a situation just like this and would
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，我们所了解到的关于警察局为什么不尝试使用黄旗法的信息有哪些，因为它显然是为了解决像这样的情况而存在的，并且

sentences.en: not force the police to rely on the informal systems that we've been talking about of the
sentences.zh: 不会迫使警方去依赖我们一直在谈论的那些非正式系统，比如

sentences.en: family, the Army Reserve, this law is there so that police can go to a judge and say, we've tried this, we've tried that, it didn't work.
sentences.zh: 家属、陆军预备役。这项法律的存在就是为了让警察能够对法官说：我们试了这个，我们试了那个，都没用。

sentences.en: Now we need to use the most formal and forceful intervention possible.
sentences.zh: 现在我们需要采取尽可能正式和强有力的干预措施。

sentences.en: Why didn't they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不这样做呢？

sentences.en: We really don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道。

sentences.en: The sheriff in Sagahawk County has defended the department's actions and said that they tried to get the family involved to take away the guns, but he really hasn't explained
sentences.zh: 萨加霍克县的警长为该部门的行动进行了辩护，称他们曾试图让家属参与进来以没收枪支，但他实际上并没有解释

sentences.en: why they didn't use the yellow flag law.
sentences.zh: 为什么他们没有动用黄色旗帜法。

sentences.en: And what we found out is that this department has never used the yellow flag law since it was passed.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现的是，自从该法律通过以来，这个部门就从未动用过黄色旗帜法。

sentences.en: In the state, it's been used a total of 81 times, but never by this sheriff's office.
sentences.zh: 在该州，这项法律总共被使用了 81 次，但这个警长办公室却一次也没有用过。

sentences.en: Well, that makes me wonder what elected officials in Maine have said about exactly how this played
sentences.zh: 好吧，这让我不禁想知道，缅因州的民选官员究竟是如何评价这一事件的进展的

sentences.en: out and what that tells us about whether or not Maine's yellow flag law is working.
sentences.zh: 以及这向我们说明了缅因州的黄色旗帜法是否正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: In the wake of this, elected officials have themselves wondered why the yellow flag law wasn't used.
sentences.zh: 在此事件之后，民选官员自己也在纳闷，为什么当时没有动用黄色旗帜法。

sentences.en: In fact, Maine's senior senator, Susan Collins, who's a Republican, said at a news conference that she thought that the yellow flag law should have been used in this case.
sentences.zh: 事实上，缅因州资深参议员、共和党人苏珊·柯林斯在一次新闻发布会上表示，她认为本案当时本该动用黄色旗帜法。

sentences.en: It certainly seems that on the basis of the facts that we have, that the yellow flag law should
sentences.zh: 根据我们手头的事实，情况确实如此，如果嫌疑人因精神疾病住院了两周，

sentences.en: have been triggered if, in fact, the suspect was hospitalized for two weeks for mental illness.
sentences.zh: 那么黄色旗帜法本该被触发。

sentences.en: And Collins is essentially saying there's a good law in the books that applies to situations
sentences.zh: 柯林斯的实质意思是，现行法律中有一条很好的法律，适用于正如此类的情况，

sentences.en: exactly like this and he should have been separated from his weapons and said that she doesn't understand why it wasn't used in this case.
sentences.zh: 而且本该收缴他的武器，她表示不解为什么本案中没有使用该法。

sentences.en: Well, given that the yellow flag law didn't seem to work, are any of the officials in Maine talking about the need for the state's gun laws to change at all?
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然黄色旗帜法似乎没起作用，缅因州的官员中是否有人在讨论是否有必要修改该州的枪支法律？

sentences.en: And I'm thinking back, Nick, to something you said earlier in our conversation about the moment that this shooter tried to buy a silencer.
sentences.zh: 尼克，我想起你在我们之前的对话中提到过的一个时刻，当时这名枪手试图购买消音器。

sentences.en: You recounted that he had to volunteer that he had been hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 你回忆说，他不得不主动交代自己曾住过院。

sentences.en: But of course, a determined potential mass shooter might not do that, might not self-report.
sentences.zh: 但当然，一个铁了心的潜在群体枪击案凶手可能不会这么做，可能不会主动申报。

sentences.en: And, of course, he was still able to buy more guns after authorities were made aware of his mental health and after he was hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，在有关部门得知他的精神健康状况且他住院之后，他依然能够买到更多枪支。

sentences.en: I mean, given that, are leaders in Maine asking tough questions about whether a yellow flag law is enough if things need to change?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，鉴于此，缅因州的领导层是否在提出一些尖锐的问题：如果需要做出改变，黄色旗帜法是否还足够？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实在问。

sentences.en: State lawmakers are talking about trying to do something in the wake of this attack.
sentences.zh: 在这起袭击事件发生后，州议员们正在讨论试图采取一些行动。

sentences.en: And the governor has said that she wants to take some action, that she wanted to, you
sentences.zh: 州长已经表示，她希望采取一些行动，她希望，

sentences.en: know, gather diverse voices from different viewpoints in a room and talk about what could be done.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，把不同观点的多元声音聚在一个房间里，讨论可以做些什么。

sentences.en: But beyond that, she has really not committed to any kind of gun control legislation in the wake of this attack.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，在这场袭击发生后，她实际上并未承诺任何形式的枪支管控立法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, of course, as we all know, state officials, local officials only have so much power given that our gun laws are so grounded in federal law.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，正如我们所知，既然我们的枪支法律如此深深扎根于联邦法律，州官员和地方官员的权力也就只有那么大。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And you did have some movement from a member of the federal delegation from Maine, Representative
sentences.zh: 不过，来自缅因州的联邦代表团成员、众议员

sentences.en: Jared Golden, who's a Democrat from Maine but has long been a supporter of gun rights and opposed to bans on assault weapons.
sentences.zh: 贾里德·戈登确实做出了一些表态。他是缅因州的民主党人，但长期以来一直是枪支权利的支持者，并反对禁止攻击性武器。

sentences.en: I have opposed efforts to ban deadly weapons of war, like the assault rifle he used to carry out this crime.
sentences.zh: 我曾反对那些旨在禁止致命战争武器的努力，比如他用来实施这起罪行的突击步枪。

sentences.en: The time has now come for me to take responsibility for this failure, which is why I now call on
sentences.zh: 现在是我为这一失误承担责任的时候了，这就是为什么我现在呼吁

sentences.en: the United States Congress to ban assault rifles like the one used by the sick perpetrator of this mass killing in my hometown of Lewiston, Maine.
sentences.zh: 美国国会禁止突击步枪，就像我故乡缅因州刘易斯顿这起大规模杀戮事件中那个病态的凶手所使用的那种。

sentences.en: He came out at a press conference very emotional and said that he was changing his mind and actually would support banning assault weapons.
sentences.zh: 他在一次新闻发布会上情绪激动地出面，表示自己改变了主意，实际上将支持禁止攻击性武器。

sentences.en: For the good of my community, I will work with any colleague to get this done in the time that I have left in Congress.
sentences.zh: 为了我社区的福祉，在我留在国会的剩余时间里，我将与任何同事合作来完成这件事。

sentences.en: He asked Maine voters for forgiveness and said that he had been part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 他请求缅因州选民的原谅，并表示自己也是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: It was a really stunning reversal that you don't see in politics too much.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正令人震惊的戏剧性转变，在政治上并不多见。

sentences.en: But of course, Golden is a Democrat in the House, which is controlled by Republicans, and
sentences.zh: 但当然，戈登是众议院的民主党人，而众议院由共和党人控制，

sentences.en: Republicans in Congress have expressed virtually zero interest in meaningfully restricting access to guns.
sentences.zh: 国会的共和党人几乎没有表达出任何有意义地限制枪支获取途径的兴趣。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, Susan Collins was actually standing next to Jared Golden when he made this emotional and surprising reversal on assault weapons, and she was asked if she would do the same.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当贾里德·戈登在攻击性武器问题上做出这种情绪化且令人惊讶的转变时，苏珊·柯林斯其实就站在他旁边，有人问她是否也会这样做。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, let me say that I think it is more important that we ban very high capacity magazines.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我要说的是，我认为更重要的是我们应该禁止超大容量弹匣。

sentences.en: I think that would have more input and more effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 我认为那会有更大的影响和更显著的效果。

sentences.en: But she declined to go that far.
sentences.zh: 但她拒绝走得更远。

sentences.en: So there, in a nutshell, are the limits of Congress's willingness to act on guns.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，国会在枪支问题上采取行动的意愿也就止步于此了。

sentences.en: And Nick, I want to end in a way where we began, which is with the reality that so many people in the story of this shooter did the quote-unquote right thing.
sentences.zh: 尼克，我想以我们开始的方式结束，那就是这样一个现实：在这名枪手的事件中，有那么多人都做了所谓的“正确的事”。

sentences.en: They spoke up.
sentences.zh: 他们发声了。

sentences.en: They tried to do something.
sentences.zh: 他们试图做点什么。

sentences.en: They called the police.
sentences.zh: 他们报了警。

sentences.en: They did something that, when you really think about it, is exceptionally difficult.
sentences.zh: 他们做了一件你仔细想想会极其困难的事。

sentences.en: They told someone in law enforcement that a person they care about is a threat, knowing that there would be repercussions.
sentences.zh: 他们向执法人员透露，他们关心的人是一个威胁，明知这会带来后果。

sentences.en: And yet, none of it worked.
sentences.zh: 然而，这一切都没有起作用。

sentences.en: Which really does raise the question of whether it's a yellow flag law or even a red flag law.
sentences.zh: 这确实引发了一个问题：无论是黄色旗帜法还是红旗法，

sentences.en: These lonely laws we have on the books are really up to the task.
sentences.zh: 我们现有的这些形单影只的法律真的能担此重任吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You had a huge number of people in this situation doing one of the hardest things, which is basically
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，有极多的人做了一件最艰难的事情，那就是基本上

sentences.en: calling the authorities on a loved one, being willing to get someone in trouble.
sentences.zh: 大义灭亲，向当局举报所爱之人，甘愿让某人陷入麻烦。

sentences.en: His ex-wife, his teenage son, his brother, his sister, his father, and many people in the
sentences.zh: 他的前妻、十几岁的儿子、兄弟、姐姐、父亲，以及许多与他在

sentences.en: Army Reserve with him, including one of his longtime friends.
sentences.zh: 陆军预备役共事的人，其中包括他的一位老朋友。

sentences.en: All these people wanted him to get help and took that first step to doing so, knowing that
sentences.zh: 所有这些人、都希望他能获得帮助，并为此迈出了第一步，明知这么做对他的后果可能并不好，

sentences.en: the repercussions for him might not be good, but that they hoped it would get him the help that he needed.
sentences.zh: 但他们希望这能让他得到所需的帮助。

sentences.en: But even after that difficult step, you still have to rely on the people who are in charge of enforcing these laws or doing what they can to do it.
sentences.zh: 但即便迈出了这艰难的一步，你依然不得不指望那些负责执行这些法律或尽其所能去执行的人。

sentences.en: And in this case, the law is on the books, and the police never tried to use it.
sentences.zh: 而在本案中，法律是现成的，而警方却从未尝试去使用它。

sentences.en: So what this tragedy has made clear is that these laws, even if they're on the books and available, are only as good as a police department that's willing to use them.
sentences.zh: 因此，这场悲剧清楚地表明：这些法律，即便已经存在且可资利用，其成效也完全取决于是否有一支愿意使用它们的警察队伍。

sentences.en: Well, Nick, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，尼克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此深表感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: On Wednesday afternoon, the White House said that President Biden and First Lady Jill Biden would travel to Maine tomorrow to honor the victims of the mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 周三下午，白宫表示拜登总统和第一夫人吉尔·拜登将于明天前往缅因州，以缅怀大规模枪击事件的遇难者。

sentences.en: In the days since the shooting, Biden has called on Republicans in Congress to join him in seeking a ban on assault weapons.
sentences.zh: 在枪击事件发生后的几天里，拜登一直呼吁国会共和党人加入他的行列，寻求禁止攻击性武器。

sentences.en: In a statement, the president said, quote,
sentences.zh: 在一份声明中，总统表示，引述如下：

sentences.en: This is the very least we owe every American who will now bear the scars, physical and mental, of this latest attack.
sentences.zh: 这是我们亏欠每一位美国人的最起码的底线，他们如今将承受这场最新袭击带来的肉体和精神创伤。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: After long negotiations between multiple governments, Egypt allowed hundreds of people, including several Americans, to leave Gaza on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 经过多国政府之间漫长的谈判，埃及于周三允许数百人（其中包括数名美国人）离开加沙。

sentences.en: It was the first wave of what are expected to be thousands of foreign nationals, aid workers, and injured Palestinians to flee Gaza into Egypt.
sentences.zh: 这是预计将有数千名外国公民、救援人员和受伤巴勒斯坦人从加沙逃往埃及的第一波人员。

sentences.en: All of them entered Egypt at the Rafah crossing, so far the only escape route for people trapped in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 他们全部经由拉法口岸进入埃及，这是目前被困加沙人员唯一的逃生路线。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Israel's military said it had broken through Hamas's front lines in northern Gaza, a milestone in its ground operation, which is aimed at destroying Hamas.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，以色列军方表示，他们已经突破了哈马斯在加沙北部的防线，这是其旨在消灭哈马斯的地面行动中的一个里程碑。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Eric Krupke, Olivia Natt, Summer Tamad, and Rochelle Bonja.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由埃里克·克鲁普克、奥利维亚·纳特、萨默·塔马德和罗谢尔·邦贾制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Liz O.
sentences.zh: 由莉兹·奥·巴林剪辑。

sentences.en: Balin.
sentences.zh: 巴林。

sentences.en: Fact-checked by Summer Tamad and Susan Lee.
sentences.zh: 由萨默·塔马德和苏珊·李进行事实核查。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell, Rowan Namisto, Pat McCusker, and Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 包含由丹·鲍威尔、罗南·纳米斯托、帕特·麦卡斯克和马里恩·洛扎诺创作的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansfork of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福克创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Chelsea Rose Marcias, Amelia Nirenberg, and Shaila Dewan.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢切尔西·罗斯·马西亚斯、阿米莉亚·尼伦伯格和沙伊拉·德旺。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日简报》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。
